title: t3229: fix OpenAI OAuth availability when env key is stale
body:
## Summary

Fixes the failure mode where a stale `OPENAI_API_KEY` (or any provider env key) masks a valid OAuth account in auth.json, causing the model-availability probe to mark the provider as `key_invalid` even though the OpenCode runtime would successfully authenticate via OAuth at session start.

## Changes

**`model-availability-probe-lib.sh`**
- Adds `_probe_check_oauth_fallback` helper: when the HTTP probe rejects the resolved key (HTTP 401/403 → exit 3), checks `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json` for an OAuth entry for the same provider. If found, records the provider as healthy (the runtime handles OAuth authentication at session start). Returns 3 with no side-effects when no OAuth entry exists.
- Modifies `probe_provider`: after `_probe_execute_http` returns exit 3, calls `_probe_check_oauth_fallback` before propagating the failure.

**`model-availability-helper.sh`**

title: t3221: setup.sh steady-state under 60s — rsync drift check, SHA-skip backup, async pulse restart, migration sentinels
body:
## Summary

`bash setup.sh --non-interactive` was taking >150s on a converged system (no actual changes to deploy). This PR optimizes the steady-state (no-op) re-run to target <60s by eliminating four classes of redundant work.

## Changes

### 1. `setup-modules/agent-deploy.sh` — `_warn_deployed_script_drift`

Replaced 783 individual `diff -q` subprocess calls (one per `.sh` file in `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/`) with a single `rsync --checksum --dry-run` bulk comparison. rsync computes checksums in one pass; the old loop spawned one subprocess per file.

- Before: 783 `diff -q` calls → 783 subprocess forks
- After: 1 `rsync --checksum --dry-run` call

### 2. `setup-modules/agent-deploy.sh` — `deploy_aidevops_agents` backup skip

Added SHA-based guard: when `~/.aidevops/.deployed-sha` matches the current repo `HEAD`, skip `create_backup_with_rotation` entirely. On a no-op run nothing has changed, so there is nothing worth backing up. This avoids a full `rsync -a` of 1233 files on every run.

### 3. `setup-modules/agent-deploy.sh` — async pulse restart

The `_restart_pulse_if_running` call was blocking setup for 10-15s (pkill + up to 10s die-poll + sleep 5 launchd grace period). Since the deploy is already complete on disk at that point, the pulse can restart asynchronously. Changed to `_restart_pulse_if_running & disown`. The deployed-SHA stamp is now written _before_ the restart (no semantic change — deploy is on disk either way).

### 4. `setup-modules/migrations.sh` — sentinel guards on expensive migrations

Three migration functions that ran expensive filesystem scans on every setup are now guarded by sentinel files in `~/.aidevops/.migrations/`:

- `migrate_agent_to_agents_folder`: repos.json scan + `find ~/Git` (`.agent` symlinks) — runs once and done
- `migrate_loop_state_directories`: `find ~/Git -maxdepth 3 -name .git` scan — runs once and done
- `cleanup_deprecated_mcps` (one-time block): repeated jq on opencode.json — guarded by versioned sentinel `v1` (bump when new deprecated MCPs are added; `update_mcp_paths_in_opencode` remains unguarded)

## Verification

```bash
# Steady-state: second back-to-back run should be well under 60s
time bash setup.sh --non-interactive
time bash setup.sh --non-interactive  # second run: backup skipped, migrations skipped

# Verify agents still deployed correctly
ls -la ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/worker-activity-helper.sh

# Verify sentinels created
ls ~/.aidevops/.migrations/

# Shellcheck (already clean in CI)
shellcheck setup-modules/agent-deploy.sh setup-modules/migrations.sh

# Pulse must still restart after a real change (delete SHA stamp to force)
rm ~/.aidevops/.deployed-sha
time bash setup.sh --non-interactive  # should backup + restart pulse
```

## Files modified

- `EDIT: setup-modules/agent-deploy.sh` — drift check, backup skip, async restart
- `EDIT: setup-modules/migrations.sh` — sentinel guards on 3 migration functions

Resolves #21964

title: t3249: guard atomic swap mv ops against set -e suppression in agent-deploy
body:
## Summary

When `_atomic_stage_and_deploy_agents` is called via `|| return 1`, bash disables `set -e` inside the function body. The atomic swap section lacked explicit error checks on its `mv` commands. A failed `mv staging→live` would fall through silently: the live agents backup was deleted (`rm -rf $old_dir`) and the function returned 0 — leaving `~/.aidevops/agents` absent while setup reported `[SETUP_COMPLETE]`.

Observed in issue #21989: `setup.sh --non-interactive` from a linked worktree logged `rm` failures on `~/.aidevops/agents.staging`, then reported agents missing and failed to copy VERSION, while still reaching SETUP_COMPLETE.

## Changes

**`setup-modules/agent-deploy.sh`**

- `_atomic_stage_and_deploy_agents`: replaced bare `mv` calls in the swap section with explicit `if ! mv` guards:
  - `mv live→.old` fails → clean up staging, return 1 (live agents preserved)
  - `mv staging→live` fails → attempt rollback from `.old`, clean up staging, return 1
- `deploy_aidevops_agents`: added postcondition check after the swap — verifies `$target_dir/scripts` exists; returns 1 if missing (belt-and-suspenders guard against future regressions)

**`NEW: .agents/scripts/tests/test-agent-deploy-staging-invariant.sh`**

9-case regression test covering:
1. Happy path: swap succeeds, target contains `scripts/`, temps cleaned up
2. `mv live→.old` fails: function returns non-zero, live target preserved
3. `mv staging→live` fails: function returns non-zero, rollback restores target, staging cleaned up
4. Postcondition gate: `deploy_aidevops_agents` returns non-zero when `scripts/` absent after swap

## Verification

```
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-agent-deploy-staging-invariant.sh
# → Ran 9 tests, 0 failed

shellcheck setup-modules/agent-deploy.sh
# → (no output — zero violations)
```

title: GH#22075: fix verify_pr_merged to accept state=closed with mergedAt evidence
body:
## Summary

Fix `task-complete-helper.sh` so merged PR verification does not fail merely because the GitHub API reports the PR state as `closed`.

## Root Cause

`verify_pr_merged()` checked `pr_state == "MERGED"` exactly. GitHub's GraphQL API returns `MERGED` for merged PRs, but the REST API fallback returns `closed` (lowercase). This caused the function to reject merged PRs with `state=closed` even when `mergedAt` was populated — the authoritative merged-evidence field.

Reported in #22075: running `task-complete-helper.sh t3218 --pr 22047 --gh-repo marcusquinn/aidevops` emitted `PR #22047 is not merged (state: closed)` even though the PR had a `mergedAt` timestamp and a merge commit.

## Fix

Changed the decision from state-string comparison to mergedAt evidence:

```
# Before (line 265):
if [[ "$pr_state" != "MERGED" ]] || [[ -z "$pr_merged_at" ]]; then

# After:
if [[ -z "$pr_merged_at" ]]; then
```

Behaviour table:

| state   | mergedAt   | Result before | Result after |
|---------|------------|---------------|--------------|
| MERGED  | 2026-…     | pass          | pass         |
| closed  | 2026-…     | **fail** (bug)| pass ✓       |
| CLOSED  | (empty)    | fail          | fail         |
| OPEN    | (empty)    | fail          | fail         |

## Tests

Added `test-task-complete-pr-verify.sh` — 4 focused cases with a mock `gh` that simulates controlled API responses:

1. `state=MERGED, mergedAt=populated` → pass (regression guard)
2. `state=closed, mergedAt=populated` → pass (the bug fix)
3. `state=CLOSED, mergedAt=empty` → fail (genuinely unmerged)
4. `state=OPEN, mergedAt=empty` → fail (open PR)

All 8 assertions pass. Existing 17 tests in `test-task-complete-helper.sh` also pass unmodified.

## Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-task-complete-pr-verify.sh   # 8/8 pass
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-task-complete-helper.sh       # 17/17 pass
shellcheck .agents/scripts/task-complete-helper.sh            # zero violations
shellcheck .agents/scripts/tests/test-task-complete-pr-verify.sh  # zero violations
```

Resolves #22075

title: t3370: fix setup --non-interactive lock/stall recovery
body:
## Summary

Three layered fixes to prevent hung `setup.sh --non-interactive` deployments from blocking postflight retries (GH#22086):

**Root cause**: rsync with no I/O timeout could hang indefinitely. The alive-PID stale detection couldn't distinguish "legitimately running" from "hung in rsync for 20+ minutes", so retries were blocked.

## Changes

### 1. rsync I/O timeout (`setup-modules/agent-deploy.sh:141`)
Added `--timeout=${AIDEVOPS_RSYNC_TIMEOUT:-120}` to rsync in `_deploy_agents_copy`. Aborts rsync after 120 seconds without data transfer, allowing set-e to exit cleanly and fire the EXIT trap.

### 2. Age-based stale lock detection (`setup.sh:_setup_acquire_noninteractive_setup_lock`)
- Stores `started_epoch` (unix timestamp) in the lock dir at acquisition
- On retry, if the alive owner has held the lock for > `AIDEVOPS_SETUP_LOCK_MAX_SECONDS` (default 1800s / 30min), TERM/KILL the hung process and reclaim

### 3. EXIT trap orphan cleanup (`setup.sh:_setup_release_noninteractive_setup_lock`)
The EXIT trap handler now kills any registered background deployment children (skill symlinks, skill scan) that are still running when a set-e triggered early exit fires before the in-line `wait` calls are reached.

## Testing

title: GH#22084: bound serialized setup wait on stale setup process
body:
## Summary

- `_setup_acquire_noninteractive_setup_lock()` previously failed immediately (exit 75) when a live process held the lock. The caller had to externally chain a `while kill -0 $pid; do sleep 10; done` wait before invoking `./setup.sh --non-interactive`, which could block indefinitely behind a stale or hung setup process.
- Replace the immediate fail with a **bounded wait loop** (up to `AIDEVOPS_SETUP_WAIT_TIMEOUT_S`, default 300 s) so a transient concurrent setup completes normally instead of forcing the caller to retry.
- Detect **stale-but-alive lock owners** via a new `started_at_epoch` file written at lock acquisition, falling back to `ps etimes` for pre-existing locks. title: GH#22056: fix empty gh_create_issue label arg when no TODO labels derived
body:
## Summary

Fix `gh_create_issue` to avoid passing empty `""` arguments to `gh issue create` when no TODO-derived labels exist.

## Problem

When calling `gh_create_issue --repo ... --label auto-dispatch --label tier:standard --label enhancement` with no `--todo-task-id`, the wrapper failed with:

```
unknown argument ""; please quote all values that have spaces
```

The root cause: `_GH_CI_TODO_LABEL_ARGS` is an empty array when no TODO task ID is present. The `"${_todo_label_args[@]+"${_todo_label_args[@]}"}` expansion can emit a literal empty-string argument on certain bash versions (observed in practice, including macOS bash 3.2), causing the `gh` CLI to reject the call.

## Fix

Replace all four `gh issue create` / `_rest_issue_create` call sites in `gh_create_issue` with explicit `${#arr[@]} -gt 0` guards, building:
- `_issue_cmd=(gh issue create "$@" ...)` — the full primary invocation
- `_rest_args=("$@" ...)` — same flags for the REST fallback

Both arrays are populated once with explicit length checks, eliminating all `[@]+` empty-array expansion risk. Mirrors the identical fix applied to `gh_create_pr` in PR #22043.

## Tests

- Added regression tests **B'3** and **B'4** to `test-origin-label-mutex-create.sh`
- B'3: no TODO labels + non-origin labels → no empty argv element reaches `gh`
- B'4: caller-provided origin label + no TODO labels → no empty argv element
- All existing 17 tests still pass (19 total, 0 failures)
- `shellcheck` zero violations on both modified files

## Files Changed

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-create.sh:200-267` — `gh_create_issue` create paths

title: GH#21928: clarify intentional pre-check rationale in _attempt_orphan_recovery_pr
body:
## Summary

Addresses review followup from PR #21902 (gemini-code-assist inline comment).

The bot flagged the `_pr_exists_for_branch_or_issue` call at `shared-claim-lifecycle.sh:276` as redundant because `_worker_produced_output` already performs the same check before classifying as `branch_orphan`.

## Triage outcome: Premise partially correct — comment was stale, pre-check is intentional

**Premise check:** The bot is correct that the call is technically redundant from the main `_cmd_run_finish` → `_worker_produced_output` → `branch_orphan` → `_handle_worker_branch_orphan` path.

**Why the pre-check stays** (not removed):
1. **Race-condition guard**: a PR could be created in the window between `_worker_produced_output` completing and `_attempt_orphan_recovery_pr` running — the pre-check prevents creating a duplicate recovery PR in that edge case.
2. **Self-containedness**: makes `_attempt_orphan_recovery_pr` correct in isolation for any future call path, not only the current classifier path.

**Why the optimization was not implemented** (passing pre-computed value as argument):
Properly threading `pr_existence` from `_worker_produced_output` through to `_attempt_orphan_recovery_pr` requires changing 4 function signatures (`_worker_produced_output`, `_cmd_run_finish`, `_handle_worker_branch_orphan`, `_attempt_orphan_recovery_pr`), adding complexity disproportionate to saving one fast `gh pr list --head` call.

**What was stale**: After PR #21902 fixed signal-3 to use `--head` primary via `_pr_exists_for_branch_or_issue`, the comment's justification ("catches search-index-lag misclassifications where signal-3 saw 'absent' from `--search`") became inaccurate. Signal-3 no longer uses `--search` primary. The comment is updated to reflect the accurate current rationale.

## Change

Updated the comment on the pre-check block in `_attempt_orphan_recovery_pr` to document:
- That the re-check is intentional (not an oversight)
- The actual current reasons (race condition + self-containedness)
- That the original search-index-lag motivation no longer applies after PR #21902

title: t3417: support glob-compressed subagent allowlists
body:
## Summary

- Adds validator support for OpenCode `permission.task` glob patterns in primary-agent `subagents:` allowlists.
- Applies the first safe compression: Automate now uses `git*` for the Git platform pair.
- Documents the reviewed-glob rule in `.agents/AGENTS.md` and adds regression coverage.

Resolves #22251

## Evidence

OpenCode's Task tool description path filters subagents with `Permission.evaluate("task", item.name, agent.permission)`, and that evaluator uses wildcard matching on the `permission.task` pattern. A local reproduction with `*: deny` plus `git*` allowed both Git platform subagents while denying unrelated agents.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/lib/subagent_validation.py`
  - Detects glob refs (`*`, `?`, `[`).
  - Accepts a glob only when it matches at least one flattened subagent task name.
  - Intentionally rejects path-style globs because OpenCode matches against `item.name`, not source paths.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-subagent-validation-globs.sh`
  - Covers matching basename glob, non-matching glob, and path-style glob rejection.
- `.agents/automate.md`
  - Compresses explicit Git platform entries into `git*`.
- `.agents/AGENTS.md`
  - Documents the safety rule for future allowlist compression.
- `TODO.md`
  - Adds the t3417 tracking entry.

title: t3544: parent-task auto-close fires on single-filed-child parents
body:
## What

Fix parent-task auto-close so single-filed-child parents close when their last filed child closes. Convert the declared-vs-filed guard from "block close + nudge" to "close + closing-comment note", because the nudge produced no follow-on action and parents stayed open forever.

## Why

Two stuck parents (#22371 t3476, #22372 t3477) have:
- One filed Phase 1 child each (#22537, #22538) — both closed.
- Five declared phases in `## Phases` section (Phase 2-5 unfiled).
- Maintainer acceptance criterion: "Phase children are not filed until the parent brief defines concrete decomposition prerequisites."

Three layered defects in `_try_close_parent_tracker` (`pulse-issue-reconcile-actions.sh:288-360` pre-fix) made these parents un-closeable:

1. **`child_count >= 2` short-circuit (line 315 pre-fix).** Comment said "1 = probably just a reference, not a parent" — that was a pre-union-extraction filter (introduced PR #21388 commit 139d50129). After GH#20872, the union extractor (graph + body + prose) only counts numeric IDs that survive `## Children` / `## Sub-tasks` / sub-issue-graph filtering, so a single survivor is a legitimate child. The heuristic now excludes legitimate single-filed-child parents.

2. **`>=2` short-circuit ran BEFORE the declared-vs-filed nudge.** Single-filed-child parents could never receive the `<!-- parent-declared-phases-unfiled -->` advisory. Maintainer never saw "decompose more" prompts.

3. **Declared-vs-filed guard returned 1 on phase mismatch (lines 333-344 pre-fix).** Even past `>=2`, a parent declaring 5 phases with only 1 filed had `_declared_count > child_count` — close blocked, nudge posted once, parent stayed open with all filed children closed. Silent rot.

Canonical evidence: cleanup_worktrees.log mtime audit shows #22371 closed all filed children on 2026-05-01 and stayed open through 2026-05-03 with no further activity.

## How (changes)

### `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-actions.sh:283-360` — `_try_close_parent_tracker`

- Drop `[[ "$child_count" -ge 2 ]] || return 1`. Single-filed-child parents are now eligible to close. The remaining gates (all_closed, declared-vs-filed augmentation, gh issue close result) are sufficient.
- Convert declared-vs-filed branch: instead of `_post_parent_phases_unfiled_nudge ... ; return 1`, compose `_unfiled_note` with the unfiled-phase list and embed it in the `gh issue close --comment` body. Maintainer can re-open and file additional phase children if more work is planned.
- Update closing-comment heading: `## All filed child tasks completed — closing parent tracker` (was `## All child tasks completed`). The "filed" qualifier reflects that close is scoped to currently-filed children, not all declared phases.
- Function size: 89 lines, under the 100-line `function-complexity` gate.

### `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-parent-task-lifecycle.sh:340-360` — B7 series

- Replace single B7 assertion with B7a-B7e:
  - B7a: declared-vs-filed branch evaluates without returning 1
  - B7b: branch composes `_unfiled_note` for closing comment
  - B7c: closing comment template embeds `${_unfiled_note}`
  - B7d: t3544 — `child_count >= 2` short-circuit literal removed from source (regression guard)
  - B7e: closing-comment heading uses "filed child tasks" wording
- Test count: 30 pass, 0 fail.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-parent-task-lifecycle.sh` — 30/30 pass
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-actions.sh` — clean
- Function lines: 89 (under 100 gate)
- 13 unrelated parent/reconcile test failures verified pre-existing on origin/main (broken harnesses, missing helpers in unrelated files); no new regressions introduced.

## Production validation plan

Don't manually close #22371 / #22372. Let the next pulse cycle (post-merge) close them organically — that exercises the new path on real data and confirms the fix works in production.

## What does NOT change

- `_post_parent_phases_unfiled_nudge` helper still exists. Not called from the close path anymore, but kept for any future bootstrap pathway. Marked as effectively dead from `_try_close_parent_tracker`'s perspective; can be garbage-collected in a follow-up.
- `auto_file_next_unfiled_parent_phase` (zero-children bootstrap) untouched. The two stuck parents have an explicit `## Acceptance` criterion saying "Phase children are not filed until the parent brief defines concrete decomposition prerequisites" — auto-firing the next phase here would override stated maintainer intent.

Resolves #22604

title: t3547: address Gemini review of PR #22605 — vacuous-close + count derivation
body:
## What

Address two correctness findings from Gemini's review on merged PR #22605 (the t3544 parent-close fix). Both shipped to main on 2026-05-03 because the auto-merge fired between Gemini's `COMMENTED` review (11:21:40Z) and the pulse merge (11:28:23Z) — `COMMENTED` reviews do not block auto-merge per t2411, which is correct framework behaviour, just unfortunate timing for these specific findings.

## Why

### Finding 1 — Vacuous-truth close

`_try_close_parent_tracker` would close a parent referencing only invalid refs (PRs, external links, unknown state) with the absurd comment "All 0 filed child task(s) are resolved." because:

- The per-child accounting loop `continue`s for every ref whose `gh api .../issues/N` returns `state == "unknown"`.
- `child_count` stays 0; `all_closed` defaults to `"true"` (no child set it false).
- Pre-t3544 the dropped `child_count >= 2` heuristic implicitly guarded this; t3544 removed the heuristic without a replacement count floor.

### Finding 2 — Unfiled-count derivation

The closing-comment unfiled-phases note used:

```bash
_unfiled_count=$((_declared_count - child_count))
```

`child_count` is a union over graph + body + prose extractors and may include children sourced outside `## Phases`, so the subtraction can produce a count that disagrees with the listed unfiled phases (or even goes negative when a parent has more non-Phases children than declared phases).

## How

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-actions.sh`
  - Close gate now requires `all_closed == "true" && child_count > 0`.
  - Unfiled-note composition extracted to new helper `_compose_unfiled_phases_note` (keeps `_try_close_parent_tracker` under the 100-line `function-complexity` gate; 107 → 68 lines after extraction).
  - New helper computes `_unfiled_count` directly from phases-section rows whose 4th tab field (child_ref) is empty — same awk pass that builds the listed phases. The count and the list are now guaranteed to agree.

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-parent-task-lifecycle.sh`
  - B7a updated: assert `_compose_unfiled_phases_note` exists.
  - New B7c-vacuous: assert close gate requires `child_count > 0`.
  - New B7c-direct-count: assert `_unfiled_count` is NOT derived as `_declared_count - child_count`.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-actions.sh` → clean.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-parent-task-lifecycle.sh` → 32 tests, 0 failed.
- Function complexity gate: `_try_close_parent_tracker` 68 lines, `_compose_unfiled_phases_note` 22 lines (both well under 100).

## Context

- Original PR (merged): #22605 (t3544)
- Gemini review on #22605: https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/pull/22605#pullrequestreview-3275019228
- Original linked issue (closed): #22604
- Auto-merge framework path: t2411 (`origin:interactive` + `OWNER` → auto-merge on `COMMENTED` reviews; correct per spec).

Resolves #22608
